correctness.rationale: For every fixed coprime 1≤k<n, the discontinuous limiting rotation G maps half-grid p_j=(j+1/2)/n cyclically by τ. On t within √ε of h=1/(2n), ε=e^{-ah}, the n-return displacement has two dominant contributions ±ε e^{∓at}, with higher sites O(ε³) and propagated error O(aε²). Opposite endpoint signs and derivative 0<(F_a^n)'<1 on that itinerary give a unique local n-cycle. Summing the period equations and using logistic symmetry yields x_{-1}+x_0=O(ε²/a), improving phase t=O(ε). Then δ_{τ(j)}−δ_j=−ε for j=−1, +ε for j=0, O(aε²) otherwise, yielding s_j=±1/2 and x_{a,j}=p_j+s_j ε+O_{n,k}(aε²). Two nearest sites contribute derivative losses aε each and others O(aε³), giving Λ=1−2aε+O_{n,k}(a²ε²). Theorem 3.3 of Bielawski et al. identifies this attracting orbit uniquely via a.e. basin. Independent high-precision calculations for (n,k)=(2,1),(3,1),(5,2),(7,3) at a=24n agree with normalized profiles (error ≤0.00026) and multiplier ratio (≈1 within 1.3e−5). No claim of uniformity as n→∞.
